author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
BDC Deploys $1 Billion Under Sovereign Defence Platform to Capitalize Quantum and Deep-Tech Ecosystems

The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) has announced the deployment details for $1 billion in capital allocations under its $6 billion Defence Platform. Unveiled at the Canada Investment Summit 2026, the strategy combines indirect fund-of-funds commitments with expanded direct equity vehicles to crowd private institutional capital into dual-use deep technologies, explicitly prioritizing quantum computing, quantum-safe cybersecurity, and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) alongside AI, space, and secure communications.

The $1 billion allocation is split across two core investment mechanisms. First, the BDC Defence Fund will deploy $500 million into Canadian and allied-nation venture capital, growth equity, and private equity funds with high domestic exposure. Second, BDC is injecting an additional $200 million into StrongNorth—its direct early-stage venture capital fund—expanding its total balance sheet from $300 million to $500 million. StrongNorth focuses on direct equity checks into dual-use security architectures, having recently led the $16 million (CAD) Series A extension into Fredericton-based quantum-resilient cyber identity developer Lastwall.

The dual-use initiative addresses long-standing capital availability gaps for Canadian hardware and deep-tech startups scaling past seed stages. By leveraging BDC’s crown balance sheet to de-risk private co-investment, the program aligns with federal mandates under the National Quantum Strategy to secure sovereign supply chains and accelerate commercial deployments across defense, critical energy infrastructure, and financial communications.
